sections.overview: Tropheus moorii is a cichlid endemic to Lake Tanganyika in East Africa.
sections.identification: It is a small fish with many local colour forms; colour alone should not be used to identify a separate species.
sections.habitat: It lives in freshwater along rocky shores of Lake Tanganyika.
sections.diet: It grazes mainly on algae growing on rock surfaces.
sections.behavior: Adults defend individual feeding territories; observations show males occupying higher rocks than females.
sections.reproduction: Females carry the developing young in the mouth for about a month after spawning.
sections.ecology: Its rocky-shore grazing links it to the algae growing on Tanganyika’s littoral substrate.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a 2025 IUCN assessment of Near Threatened.
